profile.headline: Senior Software Developer
profile.summary:
Senior Software Engineer and technical leader specializing in cloud and HPC architecture for environmental and scientific computing. I lead teams building systems that process 100+ TB of geospatial data at CONUS+ scale—driving architectural decisions, mentoring engineers, and translating complex scientific requirements into production software.

At NOAA, I've provided technical leadership to engineering teams, establishing code quality standards, infrastructure-as-code practices, and cloud-native patterns now adopted across multiple organizations. I architected AWS solutions that reduced flood inundation processing from 2+ days to 14 hours, built HPC workflows across 200+ compute nodes, and serve as technical advisor to teams implementing similar infrastructure. I'm most effective at the intersection of hands-on architecture and team leadership—unblocking engineers, resolving critical bottlenecks, and setting technical direction.

Before software, I spent six years in wildland fire with the Forest Service and National Park Service, including roles on a hotshot crew and helitack team. I led squads through high-stakes, time-critical operations where clear decision-making and team coordination weren't optional. That experience shaped my leadership approach: stay calm under pressure, communicate directly, and take care of your people.

When not behind the computer, I'm usually skiing, fly fishing, rock climbing, biking, or running around the mountains with my German Wirehaired Pointer.

positions.title: Senior Software Developer
positions.description:
Led technical architecture and strategy for NGWPC HAND Dataset Generation, establishing cloud-based HPC best practices
Architected production HPC workflow using Slurm scheduling across two hundred compute nodes, enabling parallel generation of nationwide HAND datasets with 10% improvement in processing efficiency
Drove technical solution enabling HAND FIM model to process high-resolution lidar data (1m-5m), successfully scaling system to handle 100x increase in data volume while processing 100+ TB of environmental data across CONUS+ region
Mentored several engineers on HPC workflow design and cloud architecture patterns, providing technical guidance that resolved critical computational and memory bottlenecks in large-scale geospatial processing
Established CI/CD pipeline standards for automated deployments, reducing deployment time and improving system reliability
Configured and optimized Parallel Works Environment for HAND FIM operations, serving as technical advisor to additional NGWPC teams implementing similar infrastructure

positions.title: Software Developer
positions.description:
Developed a series of slurm scripts to enable NOAA/OWP's inundation-mapping repository to be run on a cloud-based HPC systems.
Provisioned and configured the necessary infrastructure as well as provided guidance and answered questions at the Project Level on the compute and storage requirements.
Took lead interviewer role in several interviews for the FIM-C Team.
Took initiative to fill gaps within the team as well as identify and address potential risks at the team level.
Effectively communicated and collaborated amongst team members to co-ordinate paths forward and implement software best practices.
Created computational and data storage cost estimates under various scenarios to better inform management and the customer.
Supported knowledge growth and advised teammates on various aspects of the inundation-mapping repository, its runtime requirements, and compute environment.

positions.title: Software Engineer
positions.description: Responsible for designing, developing, implementing, improving, and testing hydrological modeling software (Flood Inundation Mapping) as well as providing technical expertise on best practices in software engineering.
positions.insights: Skills: Shell Scripting · Hydrologic Modeling · Python (Programming Language) · Amazon Web Services (AWS)

positions.title: Software Engineer - Professional Research Assistant (Associate Scientist I)
positions.description: Designed and implemented a C.I. pipeline using Github Actions self-hosted runners to test CMake build system, and run workflow end-to-end tests for NOAA’s UFS based Rapid Refresh Forecast System on AWS ParallelCluster.  Developed various shell scripts (within and outside of C.I. context) to install software dependencies and configure AWS ParallelCluster to emulate NOAA’s HPC platforms.  Ported an extracted kernel from the FV3 Dynamical Core from Fortran to Julia for NOAA’s SENA project.  Wrote a performance analysis and gave presentations, evaluating the use of Julia in numerical weather prediction applications.
positions.insights: Skills: Shell Scripting · Cloud Computing · Software Development · High Performance Computing (HPC) · Scientific Programming

company.name: Cooperative Institute for Research in Environmental Sciences

positions.title: Wildland Firefighter  (Hotshot Crew)
positions.description: Demonstrated competent leadership in wildland fire operations.  Mentored new crew members, taught them various fire suppression strategies and tactics as well as standard operating procedures.  Communicated effectively within the organization and across adjoining resources using portable radios to accomplish mission critical objectives.  Served as an EMT for the 20 person hotshot crew.   Led by example, actively encouraged crew members to keep a positive morale.  Fostered and maintained professional working relationships.  Developed new crew members’ chainsaw safety and cutting techniques.  Served as a member of a chainsaw team, determining width of chainsaw and hand line to hold the fire based on various fuel types.  Maintained chainsaws in the field and rebuilt chainsaws at the station.
positions.insights: Skills: Wildland Firefighting · Chainsaw · Mentoring · Team Leadership

positions.title: Wildland Firefighter
positions.description: Performed wildland fire helicopter operations, search/rescues, and FEMA assignments.  Made strategical and tactical decisions quickly and responsibly.  Communicated effectively within our organization and across adjoining resources using portable BK radios to accomplish mission critical objectives.  Trained and developed less experienced firefighters’ knowledge, skills and abilities.  Led co-workers in dangerous and stressful situations.  Exhibited positive attitude despite cumulative fatigue during long and arduous weeks.  Constructed fire-line using chainsaws, hand tools, and portable pumps.
positions.insights: Skills: Wildland Firefighting · Radio Communication · Helicopter Operations · Mentoring

positions.title: Lift Operator/ Summer Trail Crew
positions.description: Provided excellent customer service to guests of the resort. Assisted and advised guests on skiing conditions as well as general mountain information, assured the safety of passengers and the proper operation of lifts.  Built trails through rocky, steep terrain at high elevations, as well as performed general construction tasks (Installed ski signs, cleared ski runs, burned slash/logging piles).

positions.title: Snow Hydrology Intern
positions.description:
Collect and analyze snow pit samples from Niwot Ridge LTER, enter data 
Measure chemical concentrations, water filtration, pH, conductance

positions.title: Research Assistant, Biogeography Department
positions.description:
Analytical and scientific writing techniques used to compile a literature review
Calculate regeneration with dendrochronology techniques, and present research

positions.title: Raptor Monitoring Internship
positions.description:
Analyze and collect observations of falcons and eagles, enter and establish database.
Present research of different raptor monitoring programs in the USA to management.
